group: Jews paying the poll tax each year (all Jews over twelve)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

group: Jewish property holders whose lands were redistributed after the expulsion
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

group: Jews with bonds registered in all archae (Mundill's estimate)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

group: Archae delivered to the Treasury (towns)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: Delivered by 26 November 1290; the lists of 11 survive, with details of 1,106 bonds of a face value of almost £9,100, 'just under half' of the total value of all bonds (London and York lists lost). The map on PDF p. 43 shows the 21 towns. JCR-UK (background page, https://www.jewishgen.org/jcr-uk/pre-1290/background.htm) says only 19 archae were active at the expulsion (27 centres by the mid-13th century, Jews already excluded from eight): the sources differ by two.

group: Total value of ex-Jewish properties in Hugh of Kendal's account of 27 Dec 1290 (16 towns)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: Of which £677 19s 4d was paid into the Treasury by 27 December; a further £941 was still owed by various individuals (£312 paid by April 1291); Edward gained almost £1,000 within six months. London £956 6s 8d is just over half.

group: Royal grants disposing of ex-Jewish property
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: Grants went to local magnates, royal favourites, churches and churchmen.

group: Synagogues documented from Edwardian England
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

group: Areas assessed in the July/October 1255 tallages

source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

group: tallage assessed by Henry III
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: Probably for Edward's crusade; many Jews who could not or would not pay were imprisoned in the Tower of London; only £1,333 6s 8d had been collected by September 1272. Elman's table prints the same assessment for April 1272.

group: tallage received, roll PRO E 401/1567
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: Summary table (PDF p. 114): Kent £71, Herefordshire £60, Lincolnshire (Lincoln and Stamford) £60. Text: Hereford - only Aaron le Blund, imprisoned in the Tower, paid £60 in five instalments (four by his Christian debtors); Kent - Vyves of Canterbury £40 and the three sons of Salle £31; Lincolnshire - Sampson son of Magri £15 and Elias son of Manasser £10 at Lincoln, Diey of Stamford £10 at Stamford, the first two paying a further £15 and £10 at Stamford; London Jews £404 1s 3d (of which Hagin son of Master Moses £304, paid by his Christian debtor Walter de Furneus); 'two poor Jews of Northampton' £1.

group: towns whose archae were ordered scrutinised
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: Special commissioners were appointed in February 1273 to scrutinise the archae in nineteen different towns (the towns are not named in the text); a scrutiny of the king's Chest of the Jewry at Westminster had been ordered in December 1272.

group: tallage receipts paid at the New Temple, London (PRO E 101/249/16)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

About 362 payment entries, of which 40 were paid by Christian debtors of Jews; London is not in the list. The summary table on PDF p. 114 prints the Kent (Canterbury) sum as £327 2s 1½d.

group: tallage assessed according to Elman (quoted by Mundill)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: Elman's annual averages quoted on the same page: 1221-31 3,000 marks; 1233-57 7,000 marks; 1259-69 600 marks; 1271-90 2,500 marks (£1,666 13s 4d). Mundill argues that assessed sums overstate what was actually collected.

group: Great Tallage receipts, roll E 401/1568 (September 1274 - early 1275)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

group: Great Tallage receipts, roll E 401/1569 (April-July 1275)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: Kent £7 19s 10d (paid entirely by Christian debtors); Herefordshire £15 13s 6d (five further Hereford Jews); Lincolnshire £12 15s 11d (six further Lincolnshire Jews).

group: Great Tallage receipts, roll E 401/1570 (September 1275 - February 1276)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

group: Great Tallage receipts, roll E 401/1571 (April-July 1276)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

group: tallage of 1276 (nominally £1,000), roll E 401/1572
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)

Kent £120 (the community of the Jews of Canterbury); Herefordshire £63 6s 8d (the community of Hereford £60 plus £3 6s 8d to avoid the Tower); Lincolnshire £91 (the text's items - Stamford community £24, Master Benedict of London £5, Abraham of Kent Senior £20, Isaac de Provyns £5, Isaac son of Isaac de Provyns £10, Lincoln community £20 - add up to £84, so the table and the text differ by £7); London Jews over £115, paid to Giles de Oudenarde, Constable of the Tower.

group: tallage roll E 401/1573 (headed 'XXV millia marcarum', term of St Michael 1276, i.e. September 1276 - February 1277)
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: Only three payments: Simon Alayn £1 10s for debts to Isaac, Jew of Worcester; Mendaunt son of Isaac of London 13s 4d; Saunte de Stamford £8 2s 3d. (Isaac of Worcester moved to Hereford in 1275 according to the Jewish Encyclopedia article on Hereford.)

group: tallage assessed, 3,000 marks
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: No receipt roll survives; on 12 November 1278 Antony Bek was ordered to pay 3,000 marks 'lately assessed and received' from a tallage on the Jews to Reynier de Lucca and Orlandinus de Podio.

group: tallage received, sum of the surviving rolls
value: at least £5,301 8s 8½d (about £18,000 assessed in the same years)

group: tallage assessed, May 1287
source: Mundill, R. R., The Jews in England 1272-1290 (PhD thesis, St Andrews 1987/88)
comment: On 2 May 1287 (Roth, cited) all the leading Jews were arrested and imprisoned as a preliminary to exacting the tallage; Richardson doubted the imprisonment, Mundill sees no reason to doubt it. On 20 August 1287 Lumbard son of Cressaunt of Winchester was to be aided by the sheriff of Southampton in recovering debts because he was indebted to the king by reason of the tallage 'lately made throughout the whole Jewry'.

group: tallage received, rolls E 401/1584 (September-December 1287) and E 401/1585 (January-February 1288)

The first roll's total receipts were £3,281 10s 8½d. Richardson (quoted) gives £4,023 8s 9d for 1287-88. The four payments of the second roll: £645 17s 2d, £183 4s 11d, £30 and £13 6s 8d.

group: tallage received under Edward I (surviving rolls)
